correctness.rationale: Periodic mean-zero H¹ evaluation reproducer is K(t)=B₂({t})/2; its Green distribution identity fixes both normalization and trace. Three pairwise interactions are the cyclic gap terms. On the closed three-gap simplex, any boundary has one squared Green term at least 1/144, exceeding the interior minimizing sum 1/864. At an interior extremum w'(a)=w'(b)=w'(c), and dividing pairwise derivative differences forces at least two gaps equal. The remaining exact factor (3t−1)²(6t−1)/6 leaves only t=1/3 and t=1/6, with rational objective values 1/432 and 1/864. This exhausts all real triples and proves unique equality modulo dihedral symmetry. Direct 3×3 diagonalization verifies the stated spectrum. Exact rational checks from VERIFY.py passed 487452 assertions; they are corroboration, not the continuum proof.

The unrestricted frame potential bound of Ambrus gives only 3 after unit-normalization; this construction has 10/3.

originality.rationale: The claim optimizes the squared Gram Frobenius/frame potential over a constrained three-point orbit of the periodic Sobolev evaluation kernel. Full-text comparisons with the unrestricted finite frame-potential theorem (Ambrus, arXiv:1403.7382), the geometry of Parseval frame Gram manifolds (Bodmann–Haas, arXiv:1407.1663), and RKHS regression sampling (Aravkin et al., arXiv:1301.5288) do not imply the constrained quartic minimum or uniqueness. Indexed exact-parameter searches and semantic mathematical-record searches found related but different criteria. Closest historical risk is an unindexed exact Bernoulli-kernel energy treatment; an abstract-only mixed-frame-potential source cannot be exhaustively ruled out.
residual_risks: An unindexed pre-2016 source might already classify the squared Bernoulli Green-kernel three-point frame potential under another name.
The full text of Carrizo–Heineken and the original Benedetto–Fickus 2003 source were not inspected; their established unrestricted results were cross-checked through full-text later treatments.
This is a new constrained design classification, not a claim to invent the frame potential, kernel, or general RKHS Gram principle.

value.rationale: The classical frame potential tr(G²) measures aggregate squared overlap of equal-norm sample representers, and has a direct spectral-variance interpretation, so the objective is independently motivated. A natural smallest nontrivial three-site problem has a unique *nonuniform clustered* optimal geometry; the exact sum of squared off-diagonal correlations is halved relative to uniform sampling, while the normalized potential decreases from 11/3 to 10/3. The complete analytic classification shows the sharp obstruction to full orthogonality on a one-parameter kernel orbit, with transparent scope rather than an arbitrary numerical slice. This is distinct from optimizing the operator norm of the same sampling map.
